title: A story with a twist
job: A six-sentence narrative with a line of dialogue inside it
verifiedBy: Claude Opus 5 — LLM review, authorised by repo owner

rules.text: QUOTED WORDS DO NOT SHIFT. L3-M5 taught reported speech — il a dit que, and the clause behind it steps back a tense. Direct speech is the opposite: the words are given exactly as they were said, and NOTHING moves. Il m'a dit « votre sac est au guichet » keeps est, because that is the word he used. A learner fresh from L3-M5 will backshift inside the quotation, and that is this module's headline error.

THE QUOTATION MARKS ARE TYPOGRAPHY, NOT VOCABULARY. French writes guillemets, « and », with a space inside them, and it puts a space before a question mark — which this course has done since L1-M2's Bonjour, ça va ? None of it is a word: the tokenizer drops guillemets and colons as edge punctuation and they cost nothing to learn. Inside a running account, prefer the form without the colon.

THE TWIST RUNS ON THE ASPECT PAIR THE LADDER ALREADY OWNS. The imparfait holds the situation that was standing — j'étais au guichet, le sac était vide — and the passé composé takes each step forward — j'ai perdu, quelqu'un m'a appelé, j'ai trouvé. Nothing new is conjugated in this module. What is new is only that the two tenses now alternate across six sentences instead of two.

FIVE WORDS MARK THE TURN AND EACH ONE POINTS A DIFFERENT WAY. tout à coup and soudain mark the sudden step; alors que sets one thing against another running at the same time; sauf que and en fait undo what the listener has just been allowed to believe; finalement closes. They are the whole honest spend of an exit module — connectors, not tenses.

rien IS A NEGATOR AND CARRIES ITS ne LIKE EVERY OTHER. je n'ai rien dit, not j'ai rien dit (docs/58 §4). In the passé composé it takes déjà's seat, between the auxiliary and the participle — the same slot L4-M6 opened — so it is one habit covering three words: pas, pas encore and rien.

AN EXIT MODULE RE-USES. Almost every word in these ten sentences was taught earlier in this level or below it — the guichet and the votre are L4-M7's, the déjà is L4-M6's, the imparfait is L2-M10's. If a sentence here feels easy, that is the level reporting that it worked.

sentences.display: Hier soir, j'ai perdu mon sac dans le train
sentences.cue: Last night I lost my bag on the train
sentences.literal: Yesterday evening, I-have lost my bag in the train

words.note: A bag of any kind — a handbag, a rucksack, a shopping bag. Masculine, so mon sac, and the c is heard.

sentences.trap: English says on the train and French says dans le train — inside it. The preposition follows the container, not the English idiom, and sur le train would put you on the roof.
sentences.sound: ee-YEHR SWAHR, zhay pair-DEW mohn sak dahn luh TRAN. hier is two syllables, ee-yehr, and the r at the end of soir is heard.

variations.display: Hier soir, j'ai perdu mon sac dans le bus
variations.cue: Last night I lost my bag on the bus

variations.display: Hier soir, j'ai perdu mes clés dans le train
variations.cue: Last night I lost my keys on the train
variations.changed: what was lost, and the possessive goes plural

mistake.display: Hier soir, je perdais mon sac dans le train
mistake.why: the imparfait would make losing the bag a standing state rather than the moment the story turns on. A step in a narrative takes the passé composé.

sentences.usage: Opening a story with the thing that went wrong, before anybody asks what happened.
sentences.mnemonic: A step forward is passé composé.

sentences.display: Tout à coup, quelqu'un m'a appelé
sentences.cue: All of a sudden, somebody called me
sentences.literal: All at blow, someone me-has called

words.note: Three words, one meaning, learnt whole. Taking it whole leaves bare coup free and does not disturb L4-M2's du coup, which is also one key.
One elided token, so it is its own key. L2-M10's personne is its negative twin — but only with a ne in front of the verb.

sentences.trap: tout à coup and L4-M2's du coup share the word coup and mean nothing like each other: this one is suddenly, that one is so, therefore. Read the whole phrase, never the middle of it.
sentences.sound: too tah KOO, kel-KAN mah ah-play. tout à coup runs as three light syllables with the stress on the last; quelqu'un ends nasal.

variations.display: Tout à coup, quelqu'un m'a parlé
variations.cue: All of a sudden, somebody spoke to me

variations.display: Tout à coup, quelqu'un a ouvert la porte
variations.cue: All of a sudden, somebody opened the door
variations.changed: the action, with an object of its own

mistake.why: du coup is L4-M2's so, therefore — it makes the call a consequence of losing the bag. The story needs suddenly, which is tout à coup.

sentences.usage: The hinge of any spoken anecdote: the moment the ordinary part stops.
sentences.mnemonic: tout à coup surprises; du coup explains.

sentences.display: Il m'a dit « votre sac est au guichet »
sentences.cue: He said to me, "Your bag is at the counter"
sentences.literal: He me-has said « your bag is at-the counter »

words.note: The frame that opens a quotation. Its parts are already owned — m'a is L3-M5's and dit is L2-M6's — so this row exists to carry the no-backshift rule, not to rescue a word.

sentences.trap: L3-M5 has just trained the ear to step a reported clause back a tense. Inside guillemets nothing steps back at all — est stays est, because est is the word he actually said.
sentences.sound: eel mah DEE votr sak eh oh gee-SHEH. The guillemets are silent; in speech the quotation is marked by a small pause and a change of voice.

variations.display: Il m'a dit « votre sac est ici »
variations.cue: He said to me, "Your bag is here"

variations.display: Elle m'a dit « votre sac est au guichet »
variations.cue: She said to me, "Your bag is at the counter"
variations.changed: who spoke, and the quotation does not move

mistake.display: Il m'a dit « votre sac était au guichet »
mistake.why: était is the backshift L3-M5 teaches for il m'a dit QUE. Inside guillemets the words are quoted as spoken, so the tense stays where he left it.

sentences.usage: Repeating what somebody said in their own words, which is what people actually do when telling a story.

sentences.display: Je n'ai rien dit, j'étais très content
sentences.cue: I said nothing, I was very pleased
sentences.literal: I not-have nothing said, I-was very content

words.note: A negator, so it is written with its ne: je n'ai rien dit. In the passé composé it takes déjà's seat, between the auxiliary and the participle.

sentences.trap: English puts nothing after the verb — I said nothing — and French puts rien in front of the participle. The two words also disagree about the ne: English needs no second negative and French always writes one.
sentences.sound: zhuh nay ryan DEE, zhay-TEH treh kohn-TAHN. rien is one syllable, ryan, and it links straight into the participle.

variations.display: Je n'ai rien dit, j'étais très fatigué
variations.cue: I said nothing, I was very tired

variations.display: Je n'ai rien répondu, j'étais très content
variations.cue: I answered nothing, I was very pleased
variations.changed: another participle in the same seat

mistake.display: J'ai dit rien, j'étais très content
mistake.why: two errors at once: the ne is missing, and rien has drifted behind the participle where English keeps nothing. It is je n'ai rien dit.

sentences.usage: Reporting your own silence, which in a story is usually the most telling thing you did.

sentences.display: Sauf que le sac était vide
sentences.cue: Except that the bag was empty
sentences.literal: Except that the bag was empty

words.note: Opens the clause that takes back what the listener has just been allowed to believe. It takes a plain indicative, not a subjunctive.
The same form for a masculine or a feminine noun, so nothing agrees. Its opposite here would be plein.

sentences.trap: English can start a sentence with Except and stop there. French keeps the que: sauf que is one connector in two pieces and the second one is not optional.
sentences.sound: sohf kuh luh sak ay-TEH VEED. The f of sauf is heard, which is unusual for a final consonant; vide ends on a soft d.

variations.display: Sauf que le sac n'était pas là
variations.cue: Except that the bag wasn't there

variations.display: Sauf que le train était déjà parti
variations.cue: Except that the train had already left

mistake.why: bare sauf is a preposition and takes a noun — tout sauf ça. In front of a subject and a verb it has to be sauf que.

sentences.usage: The line that turns a story round, one sentence before the listener works it out.
sentences.mnemonic: A clause behind sauf buys a que.

sentences.display: Finalement, j'ai trouvé mon sac au bureau
sentences.cue: In the end, I found my bag at the office
sentences.literal: Finally, I-have found my bag at-the office

words.note: It closes an account. Not the English finally of a list — that is L3-M10's à la fin — but the after all this of a story's last line.

sentences.trap: English finally does two jobs — last in a sequence, and after all that. French splits them: à la fin for the sequence, finalement for the outcome. Using finalement to number a list reads as if the list had gone badly.
sentences.sound: fee-nal-MAHN, zhay troo-VAY mohn sak oh bew-ROH. finalement is three syllables with the nasal at the end and no stress in the middle.

variations.display: Finalement, j'ai trouvé mon sac à la gare
variations.cue: In the end, I found my bag at the station

variations.display: Finalement, j'ai trouvé mes clés au bureau
variations.cue: In the end, I found my keys at the office

mistake.display: À la fin, j'ai trouvé mon sac au bureau
mistake.why: à la fin is L3-M10's at the end of the thing itself — at the end of the film. The outcome of a whole story is finalement.

sentences.usage: Landing a story, so that the listener knows it is over and does not wait for more.
sentences.mnemonic: à la fin of a thing; finalement of a story.

sentences.display: En fait, le voisin avait pris mon sac
sentences.cue: Actually, the neighbour had taken my bag
sentences.literal: In fact, the neighbour had taken my bag

words.note: The person next door or in the next seat. The final n is nasal and unsounded, as in quelqu'un.

sentences.trap: en fait is not in fact as an intensifier — it is the correction word, actually, and it always contradicts something. L4-M4 opened it and this sentence is what it is for.
sentences.sound: ahn FEHT, luh vwah-ZAN ah-veh pree mohn SAK. Unusually the t of fait is heard in en fait, which is what separates it from il a fait.

variations.display: En fait, le voisin avait pris mes clés
variations.cue: Actually, the neighbour had taken my keys

variations.display: En fait, mon voisin avait pris le sac
variations.cue: Actually, my neighbour had taken the bag

mistake.display: En fait, le voisin a pris mon sac hier soir
mistake.why: a pris puts the taking after the searching. It happened before all of it, which is what L4-M3's plus-que-parfait — avait pris — is for.

sentences.usage: The coda that explains the twist, once the story itself has finished.
sentences.mnemonic: Earlier than the story: avait plus the participle.

sentences.display: Soudain, le train est parti sans moi
sentences.cue: Suddenly the train left without me
sentences.literal: Suddenly, the train is left without me

words.note: One word for tout à coup, a shade more written than spoken. Either can open the same sentence and nothing else changes.

sentences.trap: sans takes a stressed pronoun — sans moi, not sans je. L4-M3 opened sans; the pronoun after it is L2-M1's moi, and je is impossible there.
sentences.sound: soo-DAN, luh tran eh par-TEE sahn MWAH. soudain ends nasal; sans moi is two syllables with no consonant heard between them.

variations.display: Soudain, le bus est parti sans moi
variations.cue: Suddenly the bus left without me

variations.display: Soudain, le train est parti sans nous
variations.cue: Suddenly the train left without us

mistake.display: Soudain, le train a parti sans moi
mistake.why: partir takes être in the passé composé, as L2-M10's list has it. a parti is the auxiliary an English speaker expects, and it is the wrong one.

sentences.usage: The other kind of story opening: the one where the bad thing happens in front of you.

sentences.display: Le train est parti alors que j'étais au guichet
sentences.cue: The train left while I was at the counter
sentences.literal: The train is left while that I-was at-the counter

words.note: Sets one thing against another running at the same time, so the clause behind it is usually imparfait. L1-M10's bare alors means so and is a different word.

sentences.trap: alors que is not alors plus que. Bare alors is L1-M10's so, then; together with que it means while, and the contrast between the two halves is the whole point of it.
sentences.sound: luh tran eh par-TEE ah-lor kuh zhay-TEH oh gee-SHEH. alors que runs as three quick syllables; the s of alors links into the k of que.

variations.display: Le bus est parti alors que j'étais au guichet
variations.cue: The bus left while I was at the counter

variations.display: Le train est parti alors que j'étais à la gare
variations.cue: The train left while I was at the station

mistake.display: Le train est parti alors que j'ai été au guichet
mistake.why: j'ai été closes the standing there off as a finished event. What was going on while the train left is a standing situation: j'étais.

sentences.usage: Explaining how you managed to miss something that was right in front of you.

sentences.display: J'ai répondu « merci madame » et je suis parti
sentences.literal: I-have answered « thank-you madam » and I am left

words.note: The participle of répondre, on avoir. It takes a quotation the same way dit does, and needs no que in front of guillemets.

sentences.trap: There is no que before a quotation. j'ai répondu que introduces a reported clause and would drag the backshift back in with it; before guillemets the verb simply stops and the words begin.
sentences.sound: zhay ray-pohn-DEW mair-SEE mah-DAHM ay zhuh swee par-TEE. répondu is three syllables with the nasal in the middle.

variations.display: J'ai répondu « merci » et je suis parti
variations.cue: I answered, "Thank you" and left

variations.display: J'ai répondu « merci madame » et je suis rentré
variations.cue: I answered, "Thank you" and went home

mistake.display: J'ai répondu que « merci madame » et je suis parti
mistake.why: que belongs to reported speech. Quoted words follow the verb directly, with the guillemets doing all the work the que would have done.

sentences.usage: Closing an exchange in a story with your own line, rather than summarising it.
sentences.mnemonic: No que in front of guillemets.
